body:
## Summary

After the previous PR, the biggest remaining cost of parsing floats was copying the token text into `token_buffer`: an out-of-line `std::string::append` per float, about 10 % of parsing `canada.json`. The only reader of that text is the string argument of `json_sax::number_float()`. The library's own handlers ignore it: `json_sax_dom_parser`, `json_sax_dom_callback_parser` and `json_sax_acceptor`.

This PR copies the text only when it is asked for:

- **Lazy copy:** for contiguous input, the fast path keeps a pointer to the token in the input, and `get_string()` copies it on first use.
- **Built-in handlers:** the parser passes them an empty string instead of calling `get_string()`. They are marked by the new internal trait `sax_ignores_number_text`. So `json::parse()` and `json::accept()` never copy float text.
- **Everyone else still sees the exact text:**
  - user SAX handlers, including classes derived from `json_sax_dom_parser`, which the trait does not match;
  - `JSON_DIAGNOSTIC_POSITIONS`, which reads `get_string().size()`.
- **Keys and strings** never have pending text and use the unchecked `get_string_token()`. This avoids a 2–3 % cost on string-heavy input that a check in `get_string()` caused.
- **Stream windows (#5828):** input read through a window into a `std::istream` or `FILE*` copies the text right away, because the next read may refill the window.

Stacked on the previous PR.

## Performance

Change of the best-of-runs time against the previous PR (the first: against #5828), negative is faster. *accept* is `json::accept()` (no allocations), *parse* is `json::parse()`. Apple M1 Max: Apple Clang 21 and Homebrew GCC 16; x86-64 (Haswell VM): GCC 13, and Clang 18 with `-falign-loops=64 -falign-functions=64` on both sides (without it, code placement alone moves Clang's numbers by up to ±5 % between builds). Improvements of 3 % or more are bold.

| file | M1 Clang accept | M1 Clang parse | M1 GCC 16 accept | M1 GCC 16 parse | x86 GCC accept | x86 Clang accept |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| `canada.json` | **−17.1 %** | **−10.5 %** | **−16.4 %** | **−9.4 %** | **−21.0 %** | **−13.1 %** |
| `citm_catalog.json` | +3.0 % | −0.9 % | +1.1 % | −1.7 % | **−3.3 %** | **−4.2 %** |
| `twitter.json` | +2.9 % | +0.4 % | +2.4 % | −1.7 % | **−5.1 %** | +1.3 % |
| `numbers.json` | **−23.1 %** | **−21.8 %** | **−22.0 %** | **−23.2 %** | **−18.8 %** | **−17.9 %** |
| `long_strings.json` | −0.5 % | +0.7 % | +0.2 % | −0.3 % | −2.2 % | −0.7 % |
| `twitterescaped.json` | +2.7 % | −0.6 % | +1.6 % | +0.5 % | **−5.0 %** | +1.5 % |
| `mesh.json` | **−13.1 %** | **−8.4 %** | **−15.2 %** | **−13.0 %** | **−15.5 %** | **−9.7 %** |

The library's own handlers no longer touch the float text, so `json::parse()` and `json::accept()` gain on float-heavy input. User SAX handlers still get the text and run as before. On M1, `accept()` of twitter.json is about 2.5–3 % slower with both compilers (it stays with aligned code; `parse()` is unaffected), most likely from clearing the pending pointer at every token. The next PR makes twitter.json 10–22 % faster.

## Tests

- **New test case "text of float tokens"** in `unit-class_parser.cpp`:
  - checks the exact text a user SAX handler receives, for contiguous, byte, stream and non-contiguous input;
  - checks the trait for the three built-in handlers and that a user handler is not matched.
- **Mutation check:** if `get_string()` does not copy the pending text, this test fails.
- **Configurations:** the parser and diagnostic-positions tests pass with and without `JSON_DIAGNOSTIC_POSITIONS`.
- **Differential check against #5828's head** (string, `std::istream`, `FILE*`; M1 and x86-64): identical, including the float text in the SAX event stream.
- **Full test suite:** passes under ASan/UBSan on macOS and Linux x86-64.

## Breaking changes

None.

- **Public API:** unchanged, and SAX handlers written by users receive the same text as before.
- **Internals:**
  - the built-in handlers' `number_float()` receives an empty string, which they ignore;
  - the lexer keeps a pointer into the caller's buffer between `scan()` and `get_string()`. Contiguous input already has to outlive the parse.
  - New internal names: `detail::sax_ignores_number_text`, `lexer::get_string_token()`, `lexer::get_ignored_number_text()`.

title: Copy the text of float tokens only when a SAX handler asks for it
